conf.description: PostgreSQL Audit (pgaudit) / jsonlog dataset / json: JSON-parses PostgreSQL's jsonlog line, splits source.ip vs source.address for remote_host, reuses the pgAudit tail parser on the message key, then renames the flat envelope into ECS/custom.

conf.comment: postgresql-audit / jsonlog / json. jsonlog re-encodes the SAME server-log/pgaudit events as one JSON object per line with stable keys - no operator prefix gap, but the Elastic PostgreSQL integration does not parse jsonlog at all (its grok expects a bare leading timestamp), so this pipeline owns the whole record, not just the AUDIT tail. message still carries pgAudit's full 'AUDIT: SESSION,...' string unstructured, so the same tail regex used on the syslog-raw/csv-file datasets runs again here. jsonlog omits null-valued string keys entirely, so absent keys (e.g. detail) are normal, not a parse failure - every eval below reads via __e[...] and tolerates undefined. Order: parse JSON -> parse AUDIT tail out of message -> compute derived fields from ORIGINAL names -> batched rename -> event.dataset.

functions.description: why this pipeline must do the full parse, not just the AUDIT tail
parse the jsonlog JSON object into top-level fields
if this record is a pgAudit entry, split the AUDIT tail out of message; no-ops harmlessly on ordinary server-log jsonlog records

derive event.type/event.action/_time/source.ip from ORIGINAL field names; remote_host may be a resolved hostname (log_hostname on), so source.ip is set only when it looks like an address, source.address always carries the raw value
batch rename the flat jsonlog envelope plus any parsed AUDIT-tail fields to ECS or custom postgresql.* targets; message is already the ECS-correct key name so it is left untouched
tag the dataset (no hyphen, per Elastic data-stream naming) and drop fields fully consumed above
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
